findings.title: Out-of-range plant_id / entry id returns 500 instead of 4xx
findings.actual: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow; plant_id has only gt=0 and path ids have no upper bound)
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' for all four requests

findings.title: Journal search over 80 chars shows a raw validation error, with no input limit and no retry
findings.steps: Open /journal and type or paste a search term of 81+ characters (or open /journal?q=<81 chars>)
findings.expected: The input limits length or the page explains the limit in plain words; the error state has a retry
findings.actual: The list is replaced by an error 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength and there is no retry button
findings.evidence: SSR HTML of /journal?q=aaaa…(81) contains role=alert 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'

findings.title: Journal load error states have no retry
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section on /plants/[id]
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (server down or 5xx) and open /journal or a plant's page
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry button that refetches without a reload
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown ('Could not load the journal.'); no retry control. On the plant page the only way to recover is to reload or add/delete an entry
findings.evidence: journal.vue and plants/[id].vue render <AlertMessage v-if=loadError/journalLoadError> with no button calling refresh

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout: Saving… can stay on forever
findings.where: Add entry / Save entry / Delete entry on /plants/[id]; /journal load
findings.steps: Make the API hang (accept the connection but never answer) and click Add entry or Save entry
findings.expected: Fails after 10 s with a visible error; button re-enabled
findings.actual: useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout, so the button stays disabled showing 'Saving…' (or 'Loading entries…') indefinitely
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: $fetch.create and useFetch get no timeout option; new journal code passes none either

findings.title: Retrying a create after a timeout/network error makes duplicate entries
findings.where: POST /api/journal from the New entry form
findings.steps: Submit an entry, let the response get lost (timeout/network drop after the server commits), click Add entry again
findings.actual: No idempotency key or dedupe: each POST inserts a new row, so the entry shows twice
findings.evidence: create_entry inserts unconditionally; the form keeps the text after a failure, so the retry sends it again

findings.title: Character limit counts UTF-16 units on the client but code points on the server; emoji entries can't be saved or edited
findings.steps: Type emoji in the entry (e.g. 300 🌱), or edit an entry made of 500 🌱 (the API accepts it: POST returned 201)
findings.expected: The same 500-character limit as the server
findings.actual: textarea maxlength=500 and form.body.length count each emoji as 2, so you get only 250 emoji and a wrong 'characters left' count. Editing an existing 500-emoji entry fails with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' even when nothing was changed
findings.evidence: API accepted a 500×🌱 body (201); JournalEntryForm uses form.body.length and :maxlength

findings.title: Long plant names overflow the Journal feed at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant with an 80-character unbroken name, add a journal entry, view /journal at 375 px wide
findings.actual: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap (only .journal-entry__body has one), so the unbroken name pushes the card wider than the screen and the page scrolls sideways

findings.title: Plant detail journal silently stops at 500 entries
findings.steps: A plant with more than 500 journal entries
findings.actual: The page fetches limit=500 with no paging; the badge says e.g. '520 entries' but only 500 are listed

findings.title: Journal page shows a stale count next to the load error
findings.steps: Load /journal, then make the next search request fail
findings.actual: results-count still shows the previous count (e.g. '3 entries') above the error, because it renders whenever entries is non-null and never checks loadError
findings.evidence: journal.vue: {{ resultText }} doesn't check loadError
